top_findings: 4 industry pages are thin and near-duplicate
Core Web Vitals not measured (PageSpeed quota + no Python runtime)
quick_wins: Add H1 via the shared heading component

findings.title: 31 of 32 pages have zero H1
findings.description: Server-rendered; blog titles are h2. Outline starts at h2.
findings.recommendation: Promote page title to h1 in the shared template

findings.title: /llms.txt 404
findings.description: Not used by Google; positioning only

findings.title: Lighthouse Agentic Browsing: 2/2 (mobile and desktop, Lighthouse 13.5.0, local run — PSI quota exceeded)
findings.description: agent-accessibility-tree and cumulative-layout-shift both pass (0 of 33 axe rules failed, CLS=0). webmcp-form-coverage, webmcp-registered-tools, webmcp-schema-validity, llms-txt and ard-schema are all not-applicable (no forms/tools, no llms.txt, no ai-catalog.json), so they drop out of N rather than failing.
findings.recommendation: No fix needed for the passing audits. Publishing a valid /llms.txt would add a counted passing audit (3/3); an ai-catalog.json would add another (4/4) but only if a real agent resource exists to list.

findings.title: Agent-UX heuristic 100/100 (complete)
findings.description: render_page.py-backed accessibility-tree scan: 5 real buttons, 15 real anchors, 0 div-onclick fake widgets, 11 semantic landmarks, 0 unnamed interactive nodes, 0 inputs missing labels.
findings.recommendation: Keep this passing by rerunning agent_ux_check.py after layout or hydration changes.

findings.title: robots.txt has a single wildcard group for all AI agents (no per-purpose split)
findings.description: GPTBot, ClaudeBot, OAI-SearchBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot, Google-Agent, CCBot, etc. all fall into the same * group with identical Allow/Disallow (/dashboard, /api, /onboarding blocked, everything else open). Not a failure today since the same policy is intended for all of them.
findings.recommendation: Only split into named groups if training, search and user-triggered access should differ; do not split just to have separate groups.

findings.title: No Content-Signal directive in robots.txt
findings.description: No Content-Signal line for search/ai-input/ai-train exists. This is a preference signal (Cloudflare CC0 policy, expired IETF individual draft as of 2026-04-04); Google has made no public statement on it and does not act on it.
findings.recommendation: Optional: add a Content-Signal line to the * group once the site owner sets a training-data stance. Draft with agentic_fix.py robots; nothing deploys automatically.

findings.title: Private paths (/dashboard, /api, /onboarding) rely on robots.txt Disallow, not confirmed authentication
findings.description: robots.txt is the only declared control over these paths. Vendor documentation shows ChatGPT-User 'may not apply' and Perplexity-User/Google-Agent 'generally ignore' robots.txt for user-triggered fetches, so Disallow alone may not stop a user-triggered agent from requesting them.
findings.recommendation: Confirm these paths return 401 or redirect to login for an unauthenticated request regardless of user-agent; robots.txt is not an access-control mechanism.

findings.title: No Markdown delivery (no Vary: Accept, no .md sibling, no rel=alternate link)
findings.description: text/markdown content negotiation is absent site-wide. Optional per RFC 9110; no primary source confirms any shipping consumer agent currently requests Accept: text/markdown.
findings.recommendation: Optional. Not a current-priority fix given no confirmed agent demand.

findings.title: No WebMCP tools registered; no ai-catalog.json (Agentic Resource Discovery)
findings.description: 0 registerTool() call sites and 0 forms on the homepage; no navigator.modelContext/document.modelContext. No /.well-known/ai-catalog.json and no ARD signal (Agentmap, link rel=ai-catalog, or Link header). Both are optional, early-stage drafts: WebMCP is a W3C Community Group draft opposed by WebKit and neutral at Mozilla; ARD is an independent community spec.
findings.recommendation: Do not build speculatively. Add WebMCP tools only when a real form/transaction exists to bind one to; add ai-catalog.json only if AEOrank exposes a real agent resource (MCP server, A2A agent, skill).

findings.title: Self-referential credibility gap: AEOrank sells AI-visibility auditing but its own site is missing the optional agent-readiness extras (llms.txt, Content-Signal, ai-catalog.json, WebMCP)
findings.description: None of these gaps affect ranking, citation or traffic, and each is optional per current standards status, but a prospect running this same checklist against aeorank.tech will see the same absences. This is a positioning/credibility consideration, not a technical defect.
findings.recommendation: If a self-referential proof point is wanted, /llms.txt and a declared Content-Signal line are the cheapest to ship and the two Lighthouse already scores.

findings.title: Not measured
findings.description: PageSpeed public quota exhausted; local Lighthouse needs the Python runtime

categories.name: Sitemap Architecture
what_works: robots.txt correctly disallows /dashboard,/api,/onboarding and declares sitemap
16 of 17 real blog posts, all 5 services, all 4 industries present

findings.title: Sitemap already missing a live indexable page: /blog/what-is-aeo
findings.description: app/sitemap.js hardcodes a 16-slug blogSlugs array by hand instead of importing from app/blog/page.js, which lists 17 posts. /blog/what-is-aeo is 200 OK, titled, and listed on /blog, but absent from sitemap.xml. Proves the hand-maintained array drifts as soon as content is added without the second manual edit.
findings.recommendation: Generate sitemap.js entries from the same data module app/blog/page.js, app/services/page.js, and app/industries/[slug]/page.js already use, instead of a separately maintained slug array.

findings.title: lastmod is fabricated (new Date() at build time), not a real content date
findings.description: sitemap.js sets lastModified = new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10) and applies it to all 32 URLs uniformly. Real per-post dates already exist in app/blog/page.js (e.g. 'July 26, 2026') and are ignored.
findings.recommendation: Use each blog post's real date field for lastmod; drop lastmod for services/industries rather than fabricate one, or add a real updatedAt field.

findings.title: priority/changefreq are noise and contradict real site architecture
findings.description: Both fields are ignored by Google. /services is hand-assigned priority 0.9 (2nd highest) yet has zero inbound internal links from global nav or the homepage.

findings.title: /industries/* pages are true orphans; /services is buried 4-5 clicks deep
findings.description: Header has no nav; Footer links only to /blog, /#faq, /contact, /about, /privacy, /terms. No page links to any /industries/* page (no /industries index exists either) or to /services except one blog-post CTA to /services/ai-visibility-audit. Combined with the separately-flagged thin/near-duplicate content on /industries/*, this is the orphan+thin profile Google's doorway-page detection targets, at small scale (4 pages).
findings.recommendation: Add /services and /industries (build an index page) to the global header/footer nav.

findings.title: Other-product pages excluded from sitemap by omission, not policy
findings.description: /crewquest, /easyrep(+/privacy,/terms), /avora/privacy,/terms,/support, /bitewise/privacy,/terms are live 200 pages, correctly left out of the sitemap (topically unrelated to AEOrank) and unlinked from AEOrank nav, but robots.js only disallows /dashboard,/api,/onboarding and none of these nine carry robots:{index:false}. Unlike /checkout/success and /checkout/cancel, which do set index:false explicitly.
findings.recommendation: Add robots:{index:false, follow:false} metadata to all nine pages so exclusion is deliberate and enforced, matching the checkout pages' existing pattern.
